Let
\[
a=v+u^2,\qquad b=w+u(v+u^2)=w+ua .
\]
Then \(A=k[u,a,b]\), since
\[
v=a-u^2,\qquad w=b-ua.
\]
In these coordinates the given automorphism becomes
\[
\sigma(u)=u+1-3a^2-8b^2,\qquad \sigma(a)=2a,\qquad \sigma(b)=3b.
\]
Indeed,
\[
\sigma(a)=\sigma(v)+\sigma(u)^2=2(v+u^2)=2a,
\]
and
\[
\sigma(b)=\sigma(w)+\sigma(u)\sigma(a)
=3b-2\sigma(u)a+2\sigma(u)a=3b.
\]

Now set
\[
t=u+a^2+b^2.
\]
Then
\[
\sigma(t)=\sigma(u)+\sigma(a)^2+\sigma(b)^2
=u+1-3a^2-8b^2+4a^2+9b^2=t+1.
\]
So
\[
A=k[t,a,b],\qquad \sigma(t)=t+1,\quad \sigma(a)=2a,\quad \sigma(b)=3b.
\]

We first compute \(A^\sigma\). Write
\[
F=\sum_{p,q\ge 0} c_{p,q}(t)a^p b^q\in k[t,a,b].
\]
The condition \(\sigma(F)=F\) gives
\[
2^p3^q c_{p,q}(t+1)=c_{p,q}(t)
\]
for every \(p,q\). If \((p,q)\ne(0,0)\), then \(2^p3^q\ne 1\), so comparison of leading coefficients in \(t\) forces \(c_{p,q}=0\). For \((p,q)=(0,0)\), the equation is \(c(t+1)=c(t)\), hence \(c\in k\) because \(\operatorname{char} k=0\). Thus
\[
A^\sigma=k.
\]

Also \(\sigma\) has infinite order, since
\[
\sigma^n(a)=2^n a
\]
for \(n\ne0\), and \(2^n\ne1\) in characteristic \(0\).

Every element of \(R\) has a unique finite form
\[
z=\sum_{i,j\ge0} f_{i,j}x^i y^j,\qquad f_{i,j}\in A.
\]
For \(g\in A\),
\[
x^i y^j g=\sigma^{i-j}(g)x^i y^j.
\]
If \(z\) is central, then \(zg=gz\) for all \(g\in A\), so for every nonzero \(f_{i,j}\),
\[
\sigma^{i-j}(g)=g\qquad \forall g\in A.
\]
Since \(\sigma\) has infinite order, this forces \(i=j\). Hence
\[
z=\sum_{i\ge0} f_i (xy)^i.
\]
Now centrality with \(x\) gives
\[
xz=\sum_i \sigma(f_i)x^{i+1}y^i,\qquad zx=\sum_i f_i x^{i+1}y^i,
\]
so \(\sigma(f_i)=f_i\). Therefore \(f_i\in A^\sigma=k\).

Finally, \(xy\) is central because
\[
xy\,g=x\sigma^{-1}(g)y=gxy
\]
for all \(g\in A\), and \(x,y\) commute with \(xy\).

Therefore
\[
\boxed{Z(R)=k[xy]}.
\]
